bounded_statement: Within this case's supplied files only: the selected result's inferential claim (two-sample t-test over 48 takes, t(46) = 4.000, p < 0.001) is not supported, because the 48 rows are four repeated recordings of each of only 12 independent crickets, and chamber_humidity is constant within cricket. Recomputing the same pooled-variance two-sample t-test at the declared independent-unit level (the 12 per-cricket mean peaks, which the report itself tabulates: ambient 11.30/11.60/12.10/12.90/13.60/14.10; saturated 12.30/13.10/13.40/14.00/14.70/15.30) gives the identical 1.20 kHz mean difference but t(10) ≈ 1.88, p ≈ 0.09, which does not reach conventional significance. The reported significance is an artifact of entering each cricket four times into a procedure that treats every row as independent, inflating degrees of freedom from 10 to 46 and shrinking the standard error from ≈0.640 to ≈0.300 kHz. The descriptive group means (12.60 vs 13.80 kHz) are unaffected.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent rather than concealing: it states that each take was entered as a separate observation, reports both take counts and cricket counts per group, and tabulates per-cricket means. Moreover, because the design is balanced (exactly four takes per cricket), the descriptive group means (ambient 12.60 kHz, saturated 13.80 kHz) and the 1.20 kHz difference are identical whether computed over takes or over cricket means, so the report's descriptive claims are accurate. This mitigates concealment but does not restore the validity of the inferential claim, whose degrees of freedom and p-value depend on treating 48 dependent rows as independent.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: group means identical at take level and cricket level (12.60 and 13.80 kHz)

evidence.description: Recomputation at the declared independent-unit level using the report's own per-cricket means: ambient means sum to 75.6 (mean 12.60, sum of squared deviations 6.28), saturated means sum to 82.8 (mean 13.80, sum of squared deviations 6.00); pooled variance 1.228, standard error sqrt(1.228 * (1/6 + 1/6)) ≈ 0.640, t = 1.20 / 0.640 ≈ 1.88 on 10 degrees of freedom, two-sided p ≈ 0.09 (the 5% critical value for df = 10 is 2.228, the 10% critical value is 1.812). The take-level result reported instead uses standard error 1.039 * sqrt(2/24) ≈ 0.300, giving t = 4.000.
evidence.observed_value: unit-level t(10) ≈ 1.88, p ≈ 0.09 versus reported t(46) = 4.000, p < 0.001

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried three routes to defeat the finding. (1) Alternative unit reading: could individual takes legitimately be independent units? No — the data description explicitly names cricket_tag as the independent-unit column and states chamber_humidity is a property of the animal, constant across a tag's four rows, so takes carry no independent information about the chamber contrast; the data confirm within-cricket take ranges of at most 0.3 kHz against a between-cricket SD of about 1.1 kHz. (2) Procedure robustness: does scipy.stats.ttest_ind with equal_var=True account for clustering or repeated measures? No — it is a row-independent pooled-variance two-sample t-test, and the workflow computes df = 46 from take counts. (3) Harmlessness check: does the conclusion survive a correct unit-level analysis anyway? No — recomputing the identical test on the 12 per-cricket means yields t(10) ≈ 1.88, p ≈ 0.09, so the reported 'p < 0.001' significance does not survive; I also verified the reported take-level numbers arithmetically (SE = 1.039·sqrt(2/24) ≈ 0.300, t = 1.20/0.300 = 4.000), confirming the reported result comes exactly from the pseudo-replicated entry and not from some other computation. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py pools every take per chamber (peaks_in at lines 47-48, used at lines 82-83) and passes all 24 + 24 take-level values directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind with df = n_amb + n_sat - 2 = 46 (lines 89 and 93). ttest_ind is a row-independent procedure that assumes each entered value is an independent observation, but the data description declares cricket_tag the independent unit and chamber_humidity an animal-level property identical on all four rows of a tag. Each cricket's four takes are near-duplicates (within-cricket range ≤ 0.3 kHz versus between-cricket SD ≈ 1.1 kHz), so entering them as separate observations quadruples the apparent sample size, understates the standard error of the group difference, and converts a unit-level p ≈ 0.09 into the reported p < 0.001.
